title: Why he prefers living in Europe
summary: He visited the US in 1959 but became homesick for Europe, where he has friends in every city.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: No, I tell you, I'm glad I made the trip in 59, because my relatives were bugging me about when am I coming back and things of that sort. And I felt sort of self-conscious and I should go back and see what's happening and see my people, you know, and see the gang, all the musicians. So I did go back and with the thinking I would be away indefinitely, probably six to seven months. But after I arrived in New York for the first week and saw the gang, you know, and heard them, I went to Chicago and heard some sounds in Los Angeles, heard some sounds, San Francisco, back to Chicago. And I really got homesick for Europe. And I was convinced that Europe is for me, you know what I mean? I have adapted myself that I'm more at home in Europe than I am in the States. Truthfully. Well, that's good. That means you're happy. So I'm very happy over here and I have friends all over the continent. I know all the groups. Every major city I go to, I know the vans, I know my friends. So I'm at home and I'm very happy.
